'''Salih Muslim Muhammad''' ({{langx|kmr|Salih Muslim Mihemed}}; {{langx|ar|صالح مسلم محمد|Ṣāliḥ Muslim Muḥammad}}; 3 March 1951 – 11 March 2026) was a [[Syrian Kurdish]] politician. He served as the co-chairman of the [[Democratic Union Party (Syria)|Democratic Union Party]] (PYD), the main party of the [[Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria]] (DAANES), in whose establishment he played a key role.<ref name="region" /> As the deputy coordinator of the [[National Coordination Committee for Democratic Change]], he was the most prominent [[Kurds|Kurdish]] representative for much of the [[Syrian civil war]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rudaw.net/english/kurds/4978.html|title=More Kurdish Cities Liberated As Syrian Army Withdraws from Area |publisher=Rudaw|date=20 July 2012|access-date=25 July 2012}}</ref>

== Political career ==
=== Early political activities ===
Muslim first became involved with the [[Kurdish nationalist]] movement during the 1970s when he was studying engineering at [[Istanbul Technical University]] after becoming influenced by [[Mustafa Barzani]]'s [[Second Kurdish–Iraqi War|ongoing fight against the Iraqi government]], the failure of which spurred him into becoming more active.

He paid a visit to [[Abdullah Öcalan]], the leader of the [[Kurdistan Workers' Party]], in 1983.<ref name="ANF">{{cite news |title=Salih Muslim passes away |url=https://english.anf-news.com/rojava-syria/salih-muslim-passes-away-84327 |work=ANF News |date=11 March 2026 |access-date=11 March 2026}}</ref> After his return to Syria, he met several times with Öcalan,<ref name=fehim>{{cite web|last=Taştekin|first=Fehim|title=Why Turkey issued arrest warrant for this Kurdish leader|url=http://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2016/11/turkey-syria-issue-arrest-warrant-for-pyd-chief-muslim.html|publisher=[[Al-Monitor]]|date=27 November 2016}}</ref> who was based in the country until October 1998.

In 1998, Muslim joined the [[Kurdistan Democratic Party of Syria]] (KDP-S), the Syrian branch of the Iraqi [[Kurdistan Democratic Party]] (KDP).<ref name="CMEC">{{cite web|url=http://carnegie-mec.org/publications/?fa=48726|title=Saleh Muslim Mohammed |publisher=[[Carnegie Middle East Center]]|access-date=26 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130429104453/http://carnegie-mec.org/publications/?fa=48726 |date=29 December 2011 |archive-date=29 April 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="BBC">{{cite news |title=Suriyeli Kürt siyasetçi Salih Müslim hayatını kaybetti |work=[[BBC Turkish]] |date=11 March 2026 |accessdate=15 March 2026 |url=https://www.bbc.com/turkce/articles/c62dqvq7dxgo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260311225011/https://www.bbc.com/turkce/articles/c62dqvq7dxgo |archive-date=11 March 2026 |url-status=live |language=tr}}</ref> He was also active in an early version of the [[Syrian Democratic Council|Syrian Democratic Assembly]], led by Kurds with Arab participation, until it was disbanded in 2002 following the end of the [[Damascus Spring]].<ref name="fehim" /> He left the KDP-S in 2003 after becoming disillusioned by the party's failure to accomplish its objectives.{{sfn|Gunter|Yavuz|2020|pp=88–89}}{{sfn|Gunter|2014|p=105}}

=== Democratic Union Party (PYD) ===
[[File:Syrian Kurds Defeat Islamists Declare Autonomy.ogv|thumb|thumbtime=0:20|left|2013 [[VOA]] report about the PYD, including an interview with Salih Muslim]]

In 2003, Muslim joined the newly formed [[Democratic Union Party (Syria)|Democratic Union Party]] (PYD), becoming a member of its executive council.{{sfn|Gunter|Yavuz|2020|p=89}}<ref name="ANF" />{{efn|According to some sources, he was among the party's founders.<ref name="region" /><ref name="fehim" /><ref name="bianet" />}} Following his letter to Syrian president [[Bashar al-Assad]] in reaction to the [[Qamishli massacre]] of March 2004, he was arrested and imprisoned for seven months.<ref name="ANF" /> He was held in jail for two to three months each year until 2010.{{sfn|Gunter|2014|p=105}}

He was elected as party president (''serok'') in 2010.{{sfn|Gunter|2014|p=105}}{{sfn|Gunter|Yavuz|2020|p=89}}{{sfn|Allsopp|van Wilgenburg|2019|p=62}} After he and his wife Ayşe Efendi were imprisoned again, he fled to a [[Patriotic Union of Kurdistan]] (PUK) camp in the Gare mountains in Iraq's northernmost [[Duhok Governorate]] in 2010.<ref name="CMEC" /><ref name="BBC" /><ref name="KW">{{cite web|url=http://kurdwatch.org/html/en/interview6.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120331031939/http://www.kurdwatch.org/html/en/interview6.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=31 March 2012|title=Interview: Salih Muslim Muhammad, chairman of the PYD: 'Turkey's henchmen in Syrian Kurdistan are responsible for the unrest here'|publisher=KurdWatch}}</ref> Following the start of the [[Syrian Civil War]], he returned to [[Qamishli]] in March or April 2011 with up to 2,000 PKK [[Guerrilla warfare|guerrilla fighters]] by permission of the Assad government, and oversaw the rise of the PYD as a force opposed to Turkish influence in Syria.{{sfn|Gunter|2018|p=22}}{{sfn|Gunter|2014|p=105}}<ref>{{citation |last=Allsopp |first=Harriet |title=The Kurds of Syria: Political Parties and Identity in the Middle East |location=London |publisher=[[I.B. Tauris]] |year=2014 |p=208 |isbn=9781780765631}}</ref>

Under Muslim's chairmanship, the PYD became the leading political party and actor in the emergence of the [[Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria]]. In June 2011, he was among the co-founders of the [[National Coordination Committee for Democratic Change]] (NCC), a left-wing coalition of the [[Syrian opposition (2011–2024)|Syrian opposition]], and became its deputy coordinator.<ref name="CMEC" /> At the same time, he worked against the [[Syrian National Council]], its successor the [[National Coalition of Syrian Revolutionary and Opposition Forces]], and the allied [[Kurdish National Council]] due to their backing by Turkey and other external sponsors.{{sfn|Gunter|2014|p=106}}

After the PYD introduced the co-chair system at its fifth congress in June 2012, the re-elected Muslim shared his party leadership duties with [[Asya Abdullah]].{{sfn|Gunter|2014|p=105}}{{sfn|Allsopp|van Wilgenburg|2019|p=62}} His primary role, however, was that of an international spokesman and diplomatic representative of the Syrian Kurdish cause.{{sfn|Gunter|2018|p=237}} He met with the Iraqi prime minister, [[Nouri al-Maliki]], as a member of NCC's delegation to [[Baghdad]] in December 2012.{{sfn|Allsopp|van Wilgenburg|2019|p=179}} In July 2013, during the [[Kurdish-Turkish peace process]], he was invited to Istanbul to negotiate with the [[61st cabinet of Turkey|Turkish government]] of [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] about the future of Syria,<ref>{{Cite web|title=PYD leader arrives in Turkey for two-day talks: Report - Turkey News|url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/pyd-leader-arrives-in-turkey-for-two-day-talks-report-51439|access-date=15 August 2020|website=Hürriyet Daily News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171122055814/https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/pyd-leader-arrives-in-turkey-for-two-day-talks-report-51439 |archive-date=22 November 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> returning on three more occasions for talks between then and October 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ZEIT ONLINE {{!}} Lesen Sie zeit.de mit Werbung oder im PUR-Abo. Sie haben die Wahl.|url=https://www.zeit.de/zustimmung?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.zeit.de%2Fpolitik%2Fausland%2F2014-10%2Fsalih-muslim-tuerkei-inhalt-interview|access-date=15 August 2020|website=www.zeit.de|archive-date=13 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220513124135/https://www.zeit.de/zustimmung?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.zeit.de%2Fpolitik%2Fausland%2F2014-10%2Fsalih-muslim-tuerkei-inhalt-interview|url-status=dead}}</ref> He successfully negotiated the passage of [[peshmerga]] units from the [[Kurdistan Region]] of Iraq via Turkey to the [[Siege of Kobanî|besieged Kobani]] in Syria with Turkey's prime minister [[Ahmet Davutoğlu]] and [[National Intelligence Organization]] (MİT) director [[Hakan Fidan]].<ref name="bianet">{{cite news |title=Kurdish leader Salih Muslim dies at 75 |work=[[Bianet]] |date=12 March 2026 |accessdate=12 March 2026 |url=https://bianet.org/haber/kurdish-leader-salih-muslim-dies-at-75-317625}}</ref>{{efn|According to one source's assessment, the Turkish side only agreed in October 2014 to the reinforcement of Kobani by successive KRG peshmerga detachments, which took place between November 2014 and April 2015, in order to prevent further airdrops of weapons, ammunition and medical supplies from the [[Patriotic Union of Kurdistan]] into Kobani by the United States.{{sfn|Thornton|2015|pp=876–878}}}} He also visited [[Tehran]] alongside KDP-S leader Abdulhakim Bashar for talks with the [[Iranian government]] in August 2013.{{sfn|Allsopp|van Wilgenburg|2019|p=184}}

He was present in [[Geneva]] during the run-up to the [[United Nations]]-sponsored [[Geneva peace talks on Syria (2016)|peace talks on Syria]] at the turn of January 2016, but failed to receive invitation to participate due to strong objections from the mainstream Syrian opposition's [[High Negotiations Committee]] and its Saudi and Turkish backers.<ref>{{cite news |title=Syrian Kurds leave Geneva after being rejected by peace negotiators |work=[[Middle East Eye]] |date=1 February 2016 |accessdate=19 March 2026 |url=https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/syrian-kurds-leave-geneva-after-being-rejected-peace-negotiators |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201108124252/https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/syrian-kurds-leave-geneva-after-being-rejected-peace-negotiators |archive-date=8 November 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Atassi |first=Basma |title=UN snubs most powerful Kurdish group at Geneva talks |work=[[Al Jazeera]] |date=30 January 2016 |accessdate=19 March 2026 |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2016/1/30/un-snubs-most-powerful-kurdish-group-at-geneva-talks |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017235420/https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2016/1/30/un-snubs-most-powerful-kurdish-group-at-geneva-talks |archive-date=17 October 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== TEV-DEM foreign relations ===
Following the election of new co-chairs at the 7th congress of the PYD in northern Syria,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kurdistan24.net/en/news/4861d542-8761-4ea6-a90a-38d6eb8233ed|title=Syrian Kurdish PYD elects new co-chairs in Rojava|publisher=[[Kurdistan 24]]|date=30 September 2017|access-date=9 October 2017}}</ref> Muslim assumed the role of the head of foreign relations for the [[Movement for a Democratic Society]] (TEV-DEM) coalition of the Democratic Federation of Northern Syria.<ref name=released>{{cite web|url=https://anfenglish.com/news/saleh-muslim-released-25170|title=Saleh Muslim released|publisher=ANF|date=27 February 2018}}</ref><ref name="ANF" /> In this capacity, he stressed the message that "the Kurdish problem in Turkey and the Kurdish problem in Syria are two separate issues and will be resolved separately. To solve our problem in Syria, we have to sit down and talk with our fellow Syrians, with Arabs, Turkmens and others. Not with Turkey."<ref name=syrian />

He was re-elected co-chairman of the PYD alongside [[Asya Abdullah]] on 20 June 2022 during the party's 9th congress.<ref name="EKurdDaily"/><ref>{{cite news |title=PYD elects Asya Abdullah and Salih Muslim as new co-chairs, Syrian Kurdistan |work=The Insight International |date=20 June 2022 |accessdate=19 March 2026 |url=https://theinsightinternational.com/pyd-elects-asya-abdullah-2022-06-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251208101143/https://theinsightinternational.com/pyd-elects-asya-abdullah-2022-06-20 |archive-date=8 December 2025 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In September 2024, he stepped down following the election of new co-chairs at the 10th congress and became a member of the PYD's Co-Presidential Council.<ref name="ANF" /><ref>{{cite journal |last=Çıtak |first=Emre |title=The Positioning of the PYD in Syrian Arab Republic's Future: The Civil War, the 10th Congress, and December 8 |journal=TYB Akademi |volume=44 |year=2025 |page=135 |url=https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/4651757}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Gharib Hasso, Berwin Yousef elected as PYD new co-chairs |work=[[Hawar News Agency]] |date=22 September 2024 |accessdate=19 March 2026 |url=https://hawarnews.com/en/gharib-hasso-berwin-yousef-elected-as-pyd-new-co-chairs |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240922202232/https://hawarnews.com/en/gharib-hasso-berwin-yousef-elected-as-pyd-new-co-chairs |archive-date=22 September 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Following the [[2026 northeastern Syria offensive|military offensive]] by the [[Syrian transitional government]] against the [[Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria]] in January 2026, he denounced the [[Paris]] meeting between the STG, Israel, Turkey and several Arab countries under American auspices, where the operation had been agreed, as the "second February 15 conspiracy" in a reference to the [[Trial of Abdullah Öcalan|abduction of Abdullah Öcalan]] in 1999.<ref>{{cite news |last=Aslan |first=Mehmet |title=Salih Muslim: As long as the Leadership is in İmralı, the conspiracy continues |work=[[Mezopotamya Agency]] |date=15 February 2026 |accessdate=12 March 2026 |url=https://mezopotamyaajansi35.com/en/ALL-NEWS/content/view/302463 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260311234011/https://mezopotamyaajansi35.com/en/ALL-NEWS/content/view/302463 |archive-date=11 March 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Personal life and death ==
Muslim, a citizen of [[Syria]], was born on 3 March 1951<ref name="BBC" /> in the village of Sheran (Seyran) near [[Kobani]] to a [[Sunni]] [[Kurds|Kurdish]] family. After completing his secondary education in Syria, he studied at the Chemical Engineering faculty of [[Istanbul Technical University]] from 1970, graduating in 1977. After a brief stint in London, he worked in [[Saudi Arabia]] as an engineer between 1978 and 1990, before opening an engineering office in [[Aleppo]] in 1993.<ref name=fehim />{{sfn|Gunter|Yavuz|2020|pp=88–89}}<ref name="region">{{cite news |title=PYD co-chair Salih Muslim dies at 75 in Erbil |work=The New Region |date=12 March 2026 |accessdate=12 March 2026 |url=https://thenewregion.com/posts/4823}}</ref>

According to Muslim himself, he had permission to reside in Finland.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria-pyd-czech/czech-court-orders-release-of-syrian-kurd-leader-despite-turkish-extradition-call-idUSKCN1GB19A|title=Czech court orders release of Syrian Kurd leader despite Turkish extradition call|date=27 February 2018|publisher=Reuters|access-date=11 December 2019}}</ref>

Muslim was fluent in [[Kurdish languages|Kurdish]], English,{{sfn|Gunter|Yavuz|2020|p=88}} [[Arabic]] and [[Turkish language|Turkish]].<ref name="bianet" />

On 9 October 2013, Salih Muslim's son Shervan, a fighter in the [[People's Protection Units]] (YPG), was killed west of [[Tell Abyad]] during clashes with the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant]]. He was buried in the family's hometown of [[Kobanê]] in a public funeral which thousands of people attended.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://en.firatajans.com/news/news/thousands-bid-farewell-to-sherzan-muslim.htm|title=Thousands bid farewell to Sherzan Muslim|date=11 October 2013|publisher=Firat News|access-date=17 October 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022111823/http://en.firatajans.com/news/news/thousands-bid-farewell-to-sherzan-muslim.htm|archive-date=22 October 2013}}</ref> After coming to Syria from western Europe for the ceremony, Muslim was prevented by the Kurdistan Democratic Party from crossing the border back into Iraq at [[Semalka Border Crossing|Semalka]] to travel to a conference on Kurdish issues in [[Washington, DC]], due to the ongoing conflict between the PYD and the KDP-backed [[Kurdish National Council]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Reactions over Muslim denied entry in South Kurdistan |work=Firat News |date=26 October 2013 |accessdate=19 March 2026 |url=https://en.firatnews.com/news/news/reactions-over-muslim-denied-entry-in-south-kurdistan.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131125081859/https://en.firatnews.com/news/news/reactions-over-muslim-denied-entry-in-south-kurdistan.htm |archive-date=25 November 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=van Wilgenburg |first=Wladimir |author-link=Wladimir van Wilgenburg |title=Kurds divided over Syrian autonomy |work=Al-Monitor |date=19 November 2013 |accessdate=19 March 2026 |url=https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2013/11/syrian-autonomy-divides-kurds.html}}</ref>

His elder brother Mustafa (1940–2021) was an [[Islamic scholar]] who lived in exile in Turkey from 2011, co-founded the private Ez-Zehra University in [[Gaziantep]] and served as its rector from 2014. Having hosted a programme on the state-owned [[TRT Kurdî]] television channel and lectured in the Turkish-occupied [[Jarabulus]] and [[al-Bab]] following the [[Operation Euphrates Shield]], Mustafa was a critic of Muslim's policies and denounced PYD's rule in [[Afrin Canton]] as "communism".<ref>{{cite news |last=Faidhi Dri |first=Karwan |title=Elder brother of PYD's Salih Muslim dies of coronavirus at 81 in Turkey |work=Rudaw |date=17 April 2021 |accessdate=12 March 2026 |url=https://www.rudaw.net/english/middleeast/17042021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240518100143/https://www.rudaw.net/english/middleeast/17042021 |archive-date=18 May 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Prof. Dr. Müslim: Kürtler Erdoğan'ı desteklemelidir |work=[[Anadolu Agency]] |date=14 June 2018 |accessdate=12 March 2026 |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/turkiye/prof-dr-muslim-kurtler-erdogani-desteklemelidir/1165131 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191214002614/https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/turkiye/prof-dr-muslim-kurtler-erdogani-desteklemelidir/1165131 |archive-date=14 December 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Muslim died at the [[Chaldean Catholic Church]]–run Meryamana Hospital in the [[Ankawa]] suburb of [[Erbil]], Iraq, on 11 March 2026, while receiving treatment for kidney failure. He was 75.<ref name="ANF" /><ref name="bianet" /><ref name="region" /><ref>{{cite news |title=Salih Muslim, Former PYD Leader, Passed Away in Erbil |work=Kurdistan 24 |date=11 March 2026 |accessdate=11 March 2026 |url=https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/story/899856/salih-muslim-former-pyd-leader-dies-in-erbil}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Salih Muslim, a key figure in the political autonomy of Syria's Kurdish minority, dies |work=[[Le Monde]] |date=12 March 2026 |accessdate=14 March 2026 |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/obituaries/article/2026/03/12/death-of-salih-muslim-a-key-figure-in-the-political-autonomy-of-syria-s-kurdish-minority_6751354_15.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260314080611/https://www.lemonde.fr/en/obituaries/article/2026/03/12/death-of-salih-muslim-a-key-figure-in-the-political-autonomy-of-syria-s-kurdish-minority_6751354_15.html |archive-date=14 March 2026 |language=fr}}</ref> He was buried at the Martyr Dicle Cemetery in Kobani following a ceremony in Qamishli on 13 March.<ref>{{cite news |title=Funeral of Syrian Kurdish leader Salih Muslim, the former head of the Democratic Union Party (PYD), in Qamishli |publisher=Reuters |date=13 March 2026 |accessdate=18 March 2026 |url=https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/funeral-of-syrian-kurdish-leader-salih-muslim-the-former-head-of-the-democratic-union-party-pyd-in-qamishli/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkwzS0E0UjNOVw?lastViewed=dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMkwzS0E0UjNOVw}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Geerdink |first=Fréderike |author-link=Fréderike Geerdink |title=Salih Muslim Lived What the Kurdish Struggle Knows Best: Wait Until the Time Is Right |website=Substack |date=15 March 2026 |accessdate=18 March 2026 |url=https://fgeerdink.substack.com/p/salih-muslim-lived-what-the-kurdish}}</ref>

== Relations with foreign countries ==
=== Europe ===
[[File:Salih Muslim & Ulla Jelpke.jpg|thumb|Salih Muslim, co-chairman of the [[Democratic Union Party (Syria)|PYD]], with [[Ulla Jelpke]] at the [[Rosa Luxemburg Foundation]] in [[Berlin]]]]

Muslim was a familiar face in European capitals where he was hosted by senior officials.<ref name=syrian /> He was a frequent guest and speaker at European political institutions and events,<ref name=fehim/><ref>{{cite news|url=http://ekurd.net/kurdish-pyd-hdp-ocalan-athens-2016-02-17|title=Syrian Kurdish PYD, Turkey's HDP leaders attend 'Ocalan conference' in Athens|publisher=eKurd|date=17 February 2016|archive-date=14 July 2019|access-date=15 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190714115358/https://ekurd.net/kurdish-pyd-hdp-ocalan-athens-2016-02-17|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.e-flux.com/announcements/78967/oslo-architecture-triennale-2016after-belonging/|title=After Belonging. New World Embassy: Rojava|publisher=Oslo Architecture Triennale 2016s|access-date=25 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://anfenglish.com/news/saleh-moslem-speaks-at-a-panel-in-scotland|title=Saleh Moslem speaks at a panel in Scotland|publisher=ANF|date=15 December 2016}}</ref> inter alia in September 2016 invited to address the [[European Parliament]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://aranews.net/2016/09/pyd-leader-to-european-parliament-turkey-still-supporting-isis/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160903174203/http://aranews.net/2016/09/pyd-leader-to-european-parliament-turkey-still-supporting-isis/|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 September 2016|title=PYD leader to European Parliament: Turkey still supporting ISIS|publisher=ARA News|date=3 September 2016}}</ref>

In August 2013, Muslim criticised the [[European Union]] for allegedly failing to provide [[humanitarian aid]] to the Syrian Kurds and to condemn atrocities against Kurdish civilians in the Syrian war.{{sfn|Gunter|2014|p=90}}

Addressing thousands during the [[Newroz]] celebration in [[Frankfurt]], Germany, on 18 March 2017, Muslim said that "there is a huge resistance despite all the attacks. Nobody should doubt that the success and victory will be ours." Muslim criticised Germany for banning Kurdish symbols, saying that "Germany should have banned the [[flag of Turkey|flags of Turkey]] and terrorist groups instead of our flags and symbols because we are fighting in the Middle East not for ourselves alone, we are fighting ISIS and terrorism for all humanity. Our resistance is for Europe, for the West and for all humanity."<ref>{{cite news|title=PYD's Muslim at Newroz rally in Frankfurt: Victory will be ours|url=http://www.anfenglish.com/news/pyd-s-muslim-at-newroz-rally-in-frankfurt-victory-will-be-ours|publisher=ANF|date=18 March 2017|access-date=19 March 2017|archive-date=31 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170331120401/http://anfenglish.com/news/pyd-s-muslim-at-newroz-rally-in-frankfurt-victory-will-be-ours|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Iran ===
Muslim visited Iran on several occasions between 2012 and 2015.{{sfn|Kaválek|Mareš|2018|p=107}} During their Tehran visit in August 2013, Muslim and the rival Syrian Kurdish leader Abdulhakim Bashar of KDP-S were asked by their Iranian interlocutors to support Bashar al-Assad's government. In 2016, Abdulhakim Bashar accused the PYD, led by Muslim, of working for Iran, while Muslim alleged that Iran was "making obstacles for Kurdish rights in Syria" and called on [[Iranian Kurds]] to fight for their rights following the example of their Syrian compatriots.{{sfn|Allsopp|van Wilgenburg|2019|pp=184, 186}}

=== Iraq ===
Muslim was seen as a rival for leadership in the Kurdish movement by the president of the [[Kurdistan Region]] of Iraq [[Masoud Barzani]].{{sfn|Thornton|2015|p=872}}

Muslim boycotted the [[Kurdish National Council]] conference hosted by Barzani in Erbil in January 2012 on account of Barzani's ties to Turkey.{{sfn|Gunter|2014|p=106}}

On his departure to Istanbul in July 2013, Muslim stated that the PYD had involved both of the main Iraqi Kurdish parties, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), in discussions of the initial plan for a Syrian Kurdish interim government.{{sfn|Gunter|2014|p=42}} In December 2014, he acknowledged the Turkey-backed Barzani's "extensive pressure", albeit unsuccessful, on Turkey to allow the passage of YPG troops to the besieged Kobani, after his own requests were turned down.{{sfn|Thornton|2015|pp=875–876}}

=== Russia ===
Muslim maintained diplomatic relations with Russia and visited [[Moscow]] between 2012 and 2015, which was interpreted by some analysts as an effort to keep the PYD's external relations balanced.<ref>{{cite news |last=Zaman |first=Amberin |author-link=Amberin Zaman |title=PYD leader: Russia will stop Turkey from intervening in Syria |work=Al-Monitor |date=1 October 2015 |accessdate=21 March 2026 |url=https://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2015/10/turkey-syria-russia-pyd-leader-muslim-moscow-prevent-ankara.html}}</ref>{{sfn|Kaválek|Mareš|2018|pp=104–105}}

=== Saudi Arabia ===
During the [[Qatar diplomatic crisis]] in 2017, Muslim gave an interview to ''[[Al Riyadh (newspaper)|Al Riyadh]]'' in which he alleged the existence of an Iranian–Qatari–Turkish pact against the Syrian Kurds, describing it as "dangerous for all the people of the Middle East, and for all the humanity", in an apparent attempt to seek Saudi backing for Kurdish participation in the [[Syrian peace process]].<ref>{{cite news |last=van Wilgenburg |first=Wladimir |title=Analysis: Shift in Rhetoric Among Kurdish Politicians in Syria |work=[[The New Humanitarian]] |date=14 July 2017 |accessdate=19 March 2026 |url=https://deeply.thenewhumanitarian.org/syria/articles/2017/07/14/analysis-shift-in-rhetoric-among-kurdish-politicians-in-syria |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250517222043/https://deeply.thenewhumanitarian.org/syria/articles/2017/07/14/analysis-shift-in-rhetoric-among-kurdish-politicians-in-syria |archive-date=17 May 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Turkey ===
Between 2012 and 2015, Muslim was Ankara's top interlocutor within the PYD's Syrian Kurdish movement, which was inspired by former [[Kurdistan Workers' Party]] (PKK) leader [[Abdullah Ocalan]].<ref name=syrian>{{cite web|url=https://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2018/02/salih-muslim-syria-kurds-turkey-arrest.html|title=Salih Muslim: Syria's Kurdish problems will be solved by Syrians, not Turkey|publisher=Al Monitor|date=27 February 2018}}</ref> During an interview with [[BBC News]] reporter [[Orla Guerin]] in August 2012, Muslim denied any "operational links" to the PKK.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-19301543|title= Crisis in Syria boosts Kurdish hopes|work= BBC News|date= 18 August 2012}}</ref> His initial meetings with Turkish officials were secret.{{sfn|Gunter|2014|p=116}} Following the start of the [[2013–2015 PKK–Turkey peace process]], Turkey received Salih Muslim for talks in 2013<ref>{{cite web|title=PYD leader arrives in Turkey for two-day talks: Report|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/pyd-leader-arrives-in-turkey-for-two-day-talks-report.aspx?pageID=238&nID=51439&NewsCatID=338|publisher=Hurriyet Daily News|date=25 July 2013}}</ref> and in 2014,<ref>{{cite web|title=Syrian Kurdish leader holds secret talks in Turkey: reports|url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/syrian-kurdish-leader-holds-secret-talks-turkey-reports-140034309.html|publisher=Yahoo|date=5 October 2014|access-date=28 November 2016|archive-date=19 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181019165816/https://www.yahoo.com/news/syrian-kurdish-leader-holds-secret-talks-turkey-reports-140034309.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> even entertaining the idea of opening a Rojava representation office in [[Ankara]] "if it's suitable with Ankara's policies."<ref>{{cite web|title=Salih Muslim's trip to Turkey and Incirlik Base|url=http://www.yenisafak.com/en/columns/abdulkadirselvi/salih-muslims-trip-to-turkey-and-incirlik-base-2015919|publisher=Yeni Safak|date=7 July 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161122221304/http://www.yenisafak.com/en/columns/abdulkadirselvi/salih-muslims-trip-to-turkey-and-incirlik-base-2015919|archive-date=22 November 2016}}</ref> According to some high-ranking Turkish officials, Muslim had ties to Turkish intelligence services from his student days in Istanbul in the 1970s until 2015, when he was introduced by Turkey to representatives of the United States.{{sfn|Gunter|Yavuz|2020|p=90}} However, following the [[June 2015 Turkish general election|June 2015 AKP electoral loss]] in Turkey, largely due to the rise of the pro-Kurdish [[Peoples' Democratic Party (Turkey)|Peoples' Democratic Party]] (HDP), the peace process collapsed in July 2015, drastically changing the [[Justice and Development Party (Turkey)|AKP]] attitude to the Kurdish issue. According to the pro-administration ''[[Daily Sabah]]'', "As a reconciliation process with the PKK was ongoing between 2012 and 2015, Ankara tried to persuade the PYD to drop its hostile attitude toward Turkey, open cooperation channels and to end its affiliations with the Bashar Assad regime. As the PKK unilaterally resumed armed attacks in July 2015, the PYD and its armed wing, the People's Protection Units (YPG), provided the PKK with militants, explosives, arms and ammunition. Simultaneous armed revolts broke out in almost all towns and cities bordering Syria; whereas terrorists trained in northern Syria staged suicide attacks in Turkish cities."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailysabah.com/war-on-terror/2019/07/24/interpol-removes-top-pkk-affiliated-figure-from-its-red-notice-list|title=Interpol removes top PKK-affiliated figure from its red notice list|date=24 July 2019|website=Daily Sabah}}</ref> The Turkish government allegedly sought to assassinate Muslim.<ref>{{cite web|title=Turkey plots to assassinate Rojava administrators|url=https://anfenglish.com/news/turkey-plots-to-assassinate-rojava-administrators|agency=ANF|date=28 November 2016}}</ref> In late 2016, Turkey issued an arrest warrant for Salih Muslim<ref name=fehim/> in a move considered putting Ankara on a collision course with its Western allies.<ref>{{cite web|title=Turkey Increases Pressure on Syrian Kurds|url=https://www.voanews.com/a/turkey-increases-pressure-on-syrian-kurds/3608491.html|publisher=[[Voice of America]]|date=23 November 2016}}</ref> According to some analysts who cited the [[International Crisis Group]] for their claims, Muslim was replaced as PYD co-chair due to his more "pragmatic" attitude towards seeking an agreement with Turkey.{{sfn|Kaválek|Mareš|2018|p=111}} On 14 February 2018, two days after Muslim was put on the "most wanted terrorists" list by the Turkish Interior Ministry and had a bounty of 4 million [[Turkish lira]] (about US$1.5 million at the time) placed on his head, he held a press conference at the seat of [[European Union]] institutions in Brussels.<ref>{{cite web|title=Red-listed former PYD co-leader Salih Muslim to hold presser in Brussels|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/red-listed-former-pyd-co-leader-salih-muslim-to-hold-presser-in-brussels-127246|work=Hurryiet Daily News|date=13 February 2018}}</ref> He was briefly detained at Turkey's request on 25 February 2018 in [[Prague]], the capital of the Czech Republic,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://yektauzunoglu.com/en/2018/03/02/a-shameful-case/|title=A Shameful case|work=Yekta Uzunoglu|access-date=5 July 2018|language=en-US}}{{dead link|date=February 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> but was released two days later, drawing angry protests from Turkey.<ref>{{cite web|title=Czechs release Syrian Kurdish leader, won't extradite to Turkey|url=https://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2018/02/detained-turkish-pyd-leader-freed-prague.html|work=Al Monitor|date=27 February 2018}}</ref> On 17 March 2018, the Czech authorities dismissed Turkey's request.<ref>{{cite web|title=Czech's drop Salih Müslim extradition case|url=https://ahvalnews.com/salih-muslim/czechs-drop-salih-muslim-extradition-case|work=Ahval News|date=18 March 2018|access-date=18 March 2018|archive-date=5 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180705233916/https://ahvalnews.com/salih-muslim/czechs-drop-salih-muslim-extradition-case|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In a February 2018 interview, Muslim said that "when I look back, I conclude that Turkey was never sincere about wanting to make peace with the Kurds. Had Turkey reached out to the Kurds, worked with the Kurds, it would have become the most powerful country in the Middle East."<ref name=syrian />
